title: Tree zigzag nerves are filtered colimits over finite subtrees
statement:
Let $T$ be a small oriented tree: its underlying undirected graph is nonempty and has a unique finite simple path between any two vertices, and each edge is assigned one direction. Let $C_T$ be its free path category, whose arrows are finite composable directed edge words and whose identities are empty words. For a finite word $w$ in $+,-$, let $Z_w^{C_T}(x,y)$ have the meaning of [def-coef-zigzag-homotopy-calculus] for the pair $(C_T,C_T)$; identity horizontal arrows are allowed. Fix a vertex $x$. Let $\mathcal F_x(T)$ be the poset of finite connected subtrees $S\subseteq T$ containing $x$, ordered by inclusion, including the singleton subtree $\{x\}$. This is a small nonempty filtered category. Subtree inclusions induce degreewise injective maps between the nerves of the fixed-word zigzag categories. The resulting canonical map is an isomorphism of simplicial sets
$$\varinjlim_{S\in\mathcal F_x(T)}NZ_w^{C_S}(x,x)\ \xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }\ NZ_w^{C_T}(x,x).$$
Here the colimit is computed degreewise in sets as in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Section 5.8(iii), printed p.25: the reduction to finite diagrams, made explicit as a finite-subtree colimit. This auxiliary formulation is agent supplied; no Stacks tag states it.

proof.text: The poset $\mathcal F_x(T)$ is small because it is a collection of subsets of the small vertex set of $T$. It is nonempty because it contains the singleton subtree $\{x\}$. Given finite connected subtrees $S_1,\ldots,S_r$ containing $x$, take the union of the finitely many unique finite paths in $T$ joining $x$ to every vertex of every $S_i$. This union is a finite connected subtree containing all $S_i$, hence an upper bound. For a pair of inclusions there is at most one morphism, and inclusions are equalized automatically; therefore this nonempty poset is filtered in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Section 5.8(iii), finite-subdiagram reduction; finite connected support in a tree made explicit.

proof.text: An $n$-simplex of $NZ_w^{C_T}(x,x)$ is a string of $n$ composable morphisms in the zigzag category [def-coef-zigzag-homotopy-calculus]. Each morphism contains finitely many diagram vertices, finitely many vertical arrows, and finitely many finite path words in $T$; the fixed zigzag word contributes only finitely many horizontal positions. Hence the whole string uses a finite set of vertices and edges of $T$. Adjoin to that finite support all vertices and edges on the unique finite paths from $x$ to its vertices. The result is a finite connected subtree $S$ containing $x$. Every path word and every commuting square in the simplex lies in the free path category $C_S$, so the simplex is the image of an $n$-simplex of $NZ_w^{C_S}(x,x)$. This also covers identity horizontal arrows, whose support is empty.

source.place: Section 5.8(iii), reduction of a finite zigzag diagram to a finite subdiagram.

proof.text: For every inclusion $S\subseteq S'$ in $\mathcal F_x(T)$, the induced map $C_S\to C_{S'}$ is injective on vertices and on finite directed edge words, hence on each object and morphism set of the fixed-word zigzag categories; applying the ordinary nerve gives a degreewise injective map. Thus the maps form a diagram of simplicial sets and the canonical map from its degreewise colimit is defined. If two simplices from $S$ and $S'$ have the same image in $NZ_w^{C_T}(x,x)$, their finitely many data can be placed in one finite connected subtree $U$ containing $x$ and containing both $S$ and $S'$ (take the finite union of paths from $x$ to the vertices of $S\cup S'$). The two images in $NZ_w^{C_U}(x,x)$ are then equal because the inclusion into $C_T$ is injective on all finite path words and commuting diagrams. By the equality clause of [lem-coef-small-set-colimit-quotient], these are exactly the identifications made in the degreewise colimit.

source.place: Section 5.8(iii), compatibility of finite subdiagram inclusions; finite support comparison.

proof.text: Fix $n$. Step 2 proves surjectivity of the canonical degree-$n$ map: every $n$-simplex of the target comes from some finite subtree. Step 3 proves injectivity: two representatives have equal images exactly when they agree after passage to a common upper subtree, which is the equivalence relation presented by the set colimit quotient [lem-coef-small-set-colimit-quotient]. Therefore the degree-$n$ map is a bijection for every $n$. The bijections commute with every simplicial face and degeneracy, since all structure maps are induced by restriction of the same nerve operations and the colimit cocone maps. Consequently the canonical map of simplicial sets is an isomorphism. The construction is the finite-subtree colimit formulation of the finite-diagram reduction in Dwyer--Kan Section 5.8(iii).
